title: Definition versions: change a cyclotron's question or classifiers without losing history
description:
Today a store refuses a changed CyclotronDefinition, and DecisionFlywheel refuses a changed task (question, labels, input field), so an application cannot change a classifier's question or add and remove classifiers without starting a new store. Applications seed the first rubric from their own parameters (Papyrus: publication doctrine), never the question, so routine parameter edits go through the rubric; this task covers the rarer structural change.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cyclotron.open accepts a new definition revision for an existing store when the application says so explicitly; it records the revision, its fingerprint, and what changed.
- Changing a classifier's question or labels starts a new classifier lineage inside the store; earlier decisions, reviews and versions stay readable and keep their original revision.
- Adding a classifier starts it with no labels; removing one stops deciding with it but keeps its history.
- Reviews of items decided under an earlier revision are not silently reused as labels for a changed question; the application can replay them explicitly.
- status() reports a lastChange of kind definition with the revision and a summary.
- No model call happens while opening a new revision; specs cover each case.
